scale_note: Real size. The shape is from your tape photo (about ±1 mm), with the S-bend at 12° as in your first print. The wire is printed at 5.53 mm like your steel hook; the pin at 6.1 mm. The board uses your measured 1/4" holes on 1" centres; its thickness is the listing's 0.155". The model may look like it touches the hole edges: that's a perfectly flush hang, and the real hook rocks in fine.
notes_title: What changed, and what to check
notes: v7: wire back to 5.53 mm like v4 (which went in easily); a rock-in simulation says v6's 6.1 mm wire can't get through the hole on this S-bend. The pin is 6.1 mm to take up the looseness. Earlier: v6: back to the 12° S-bend from your first print (the level step in v5 was much harder to get in; the slope guides the hook as it rocks in), and the wire goes from 5.9 to 6.1 mm because 5.9 was still loose. Bends are a touch rounder (3.5 mm) so the thicker wire stays clean. Check when you reprint: (1) goes in as easily as the first one? (2) snug now? To settle the diameter for good, print the peg gauge in the pegboard-fit-test project.
